doc.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: First night at Hamilton and meeting Derry Hall
summary: He hears pianist Derry Hall his first night, plays with him, then meets Emerson and the Catatonic Five forms.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So that all sort of fell together. And I can remember that first night I was at Hamilton I heard somebody over at what we used to call Silliman Hall playing the piano, and it was Derry Hall.

Derry Hall. And Derry went to Hamilton and actually played with some of the jazz bands there and actually was a guy who played piano for us at Carnegie Hall with the Catatonic Five. But I took my horn over there and he was very nice to me. He’d just graduated that
year or a year before, and we played a little bit and then I met Emerson and the Catatonic Five came together and that’s how it all happened.
Now what’s the history — do you know about the history of the name the Catatonic Five?
